title: What Is a Volcano
keyIdea: A volcano is a mountain or hill with a hole (vent) where hot melted rock from under the ground can come out. Melted rock under the ground is magma. When it flows out it is called lava. An eruption is when magma, ash or gas bursts out.
familyTip: Look at a picture of a volcano together. Point to the crater at the top and ask: 'Is the hot rock still under the ground (magma) or on the surface (lava)?'

visual.caption: Magma, lava, or neither? Drag each clue, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: build a volcano cutaway, fill magma, erupt lava, label crater and ash, sort magma vs lava, and catch mix-ups.

kid: A volcano is a special mountain. It has a hole where hot melted rock can come out.
Magma is hot melted rock still under the ground. When it comes out, we call it lava.
An eruption is when magma, ash or gas bursts out of the volcano.
The crater is the bowl-shaped hole at the top. Ash is fine dusty rock that can shoot into the air.
adult: Ages 5 to 7 earth science: volcano, vent, crater, magma, lava, eruption, ash. Magma stays under the ground. Lava is magma that has reached the surface.

Common mistakes: calling all hot rock lava even when it is still under the ground; thinking every mountain is a volcano; saying volcanoes are only fire or smoke with no melted rock; mixing ash with ordinary dust from a shelf.

In the lab your child builds a simple cross-section, fills the pipe with magma, erupts lava down the slope, labels the crater and ash, sorts magma from lava, then faces challenge traps for those slips.

choices: a mountain with a hole for hot melted rock
practice.hint: Think about a vent where melted rock can come out.
practice.explain: A volcano has a vent where magma can erupt. Ordinary hills and toys are not volcanoes.

practice.hint: Where is the melted rock before it erupts?
practice.explain: Magma is under the ground. Once it flows out it is called lava.

practice.prompt: A diagram labels {n} magma spots and {k} lava spots. How many magma spots?
practice.explain: There are {n} magma spots. The {k} lava spots are separate.

practice.prompt: An eruption sends out {n} ash clouds. {k} have already blown away. How many are left to watch?
practice.hint: Subtract the ones that blew away.

choices: magma that has reached the surface
practice.hint: Lava is what we call melted rock after it comes out.
practice.explain: When magma reaches the surface it is called lava. Rain and ordinary mountains are not lava.

pool.prompt: The bowl-shaped hole at the top is the…
pool.hint: Look at the top of the volcano.
pool.explain: The crater is the bowl at the top around the vent.

choices: magma, ash or gas bursts out
pool.hint: What comes out of the vent suddenly?
pool.explain: An eruption is magma, ash or gas bursting out of the volcano.

choices: fine dusty rock from the eruption
pool.hint: Ash is made when rock is blasted into fine bits.
pool.explain: Volcanic ash is fine rock from the eruption, not ordinary house dust.

choices: magma is under the ground; lava is on the surface
lava stays under the ground forever
pool.hint: Name changes when melted rock comes out.
pool.explain: Magma is underground. On the surface the same melted rock is called lava.

pool.prompt: A model shows {n} volcano vents. How many vents?
pool.hint: Count the vents on the model.
pool.explain: The model shows {n} vents — holes where magma can come out.

pool.prompt: {n} slopes each show {k} lava flows. How many lava flows in all?

choices: is not a volcano unless it has a vent for melted rock
pool.hint: Volcanoes need a vent linked to magma.
pool.explain: Only mountains with a vent for magma are volcanoes. Height alone is not enough.

pool.prompt: Why cool lava turns to hard rock?
pool.hint: Hot melted rock hardens when it cools.
pool.explain: Lava cools, loses heat, and becomes solid rock. It does not become rain or plastic.
